newsitem.title: USA: Camco, GF Bancorp to merge.
newsitem.headline: Camco, GF Bancorp to merge.

text.p: Camco Financial Corp said late Monday that it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire GF Bancorp Inc.
Under the terms of the agreement, Camco will exchange 1.616 shares of its common stock for each of the 292,958 outstanding shares of GF Bancorp stock, subject to possible adjustment.

Based on Camco's closing price of $18.75 on July 25, and assuming the exercise of all of GF Bancorp's outstanding options, the transaction would be valued at $30.30 per share of GF Bancorp stock, or about $9.7 million, the companies said.

The merger, which will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, is expected to be consummated no later than the first quarter of 1998, pending approval by GF Bancorp's shareholders, regulatory approval and other customary conditions of closing, they said.
The transaction is expected to be a "tax-free" reorganization for federal income tax purposes.
Camco specializes in community banking, mortgage banking, and title services through offices in Ohio, Kentucky and West Virginia.

GF Bancorp, the parent company of Germantown Federal Savings Bank, has offices in Germantown and New Lebanon, Ohio. Germantown Federal Savings Bank will be merged into First Federal Savings Bank of Washington Court House, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Camco, the companies said.

If the average of the daily average between the closing bid and asked prices of Camco for the 20 consecutive trading days ending three trading days prior to closing is above $20.99, the exchange ratio will be adjusted downward to give an equivalent value of $33.93 per GF Bancorp share, the companies said.
If the average price of Camco is below $15.51 per share, the exchange ratio will be adjusted upward to give an equivalent value of $25.08 per GF Bancorp share.

If Camco's average price is above $23.73, GF Bancorp will have the right to terminate the agreement, they said. And if the average price of Camco is below $12.78 per share, the agreement would be terminated.
